title: Patient safety incident
description: A report of a patient safety event (an incident that reached the patient, a near miss or an unsafe condition), with its harm assessment, contributing factors, immediate actions, notifications and investigation. Informed by the AHRQ Common Formats for Event Reporting and the WHO Conceptual Framework for the International Classification for Patient Safety (ICPS). Designed to carry as little protected health information as possible: there are no fields for patient names, dates of birth or medical record numbers, only an opaque reference into the source system. Records are still not de-identified data: event dates and the facility can identify a patient, and free text can hold anything, so treat them as confidential.

$schema.title: Schema
$schema.description: The $id of this schema, so readers can tell what the record is.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this format the record follows.

id.description: This report's identifier, unique within the system that created it.

externalIds.title: External identifiers
externalIds.description: Ids for this report in other systems (incident reporting tool, PSO submission, risk management).

updatedAt.description: When the record was last changed.

id.description: Identifier for this item, unique within the record.

type.title: Facility type
type.description: hospital, ambulatory-surgery-center, clinic, long-term-care, behavioral-health, pharmacy, home-health, emergency-medical-services or other.

identifiers.title: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Facility identifiers such as a CMS Certification Number or a national provider id.

event.title: Event
event.description: When and where the event happened.

occurredAtPrecision.title: Occurrence time precision
occurredAtPrecision.description: exact, approximate or unknown. Use approximate when the time was estimated after the fact.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where in the facility the event happened.

type.title: Location type
type.description: inpatient-unit, intensive-care, emergency-department, operating-room, procedure-area, labor-and-delivery, outpatient-area, pharmacy, laboratory, imaging, patient-home, transport, common-area or other.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The unit or department name, for example 4 West Medical.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: More precise location, for example bathroom of room 12.

eventType.title: Event type
eventType.description: incident (reached the patient, whether or not it caused harm), near-miss (did not reach the patient) or unsafe-condition (a circumstance that increases the chance of an event). These follow the AHRQ Common Formats event types.

eventCategory.title: Event category
eventCategory.description: The clinical area of the event, following the AHRQ Common Formats event-specific categories: blood-or-blood-product, device-or-medical-supply, fall, healthcare-associated-infection, medication-or-other-substance, perinatal, pressure-injury, surgery-or-anesthesia, venous-thromboembolism, or other.

eventSubcategory.title: Event subcategory
eventSubcategory.description: A finer classification in the reporting organization's own terms, for example wrong dose.

description.title: Description
description.description: What happened, in the reporter's words. Do not include patient names, dates of birth, record numbers or other direct identifiers.

patient.title: Patient
patient.description: De-identified facts about the patient involved, when the event involved one. Holds no direct identifiers by design.

ageBand.title: Age band
ageBand.description: neonate (0-28 days), infant (29 days to 1 year), child (1-12), adolescent (13-17), adult-18-44, adult-45-64, adult-65-84, adult-85-plus or unknown.

encounterRef.title: Encounter reference
encounterRef.description: An opaque key that lets authorized staff find the encounter in the source system. Not a medical record number.

reachedPatient.title: Reached the patient
reachedPatient.description: Whether the event reached the patient.

harm.title: Harm
harm.description: The assessed harm to the patient, using the concepts of the AHRQ Common Formats Harm Scale.

level.title: Harm level
level.description: death, severe-harm, moderate-harm, mild-harm, no-harm or unknown.

additionalTreatment.title: Additional treatment
additionalTreatment.description: Whether the patient needed treatment because of the event.

contributingFactors.title: Contributing factors
contributingFactors.description: Circumstances that contributed to the event.

category.title: Category
category.description: communication, handoff, staffing, training, policy-or-procedure, equipment-or-device, environment, patient-factors, task-factors, team-factors, organizational-culture, labeling-or-packaging, information-system or other.

immediateActions.title: Immediate actions
immediateActions.description: What was done straight away to care for the patient and make the situation safe.

takenByRole.title: Taken by (role)
takenByRole.description: The role of the person who acted, for example charge nurse.

reporter.title: Reporter
reporter.description: Who reported the event. Reports may be anonymous; an anonymous report carries no contact details, and systems should also keep the reporter's name out of statusHistory and auditTrail.

anonymous.title: Anonymous
anonymous.description: Whether the reporter chose to stay anonymous.

role.title: Role
role.description: physician, advanced-practice-provider, nurse, pharmacist, other-clinician, non-clinical-staff, patient-or-family or other.

contact.description: How to reach the reporter. Not allowed when the report is anonymous.

wantsFeedback.title: Wants feedback
wantsFeedback.description: Whether the reporter asked to hear what came of the report.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Who was told about the event, when and how.

recipient.title: Recipient
recipient.description: patient-or-family, attending-clinician, unit-leadership, risk-management, patient-safety-officer, regulatory-agency, patient-safety-organization, accreditation-body, manufacturer, insurer or other.

recipientName.title: Recipient name
recipientName.description: The named agency, body or person, where relevant, for example a state health department.

method.title: Method
method.description: in-person, phone, letter, email, portal or other.

requiredByRule.title: Required by rule
requiredByRule.description: Whether a law, regulation or policy required this notification.

ruleReference.title: Rule reference
ruleReference.description: The rule that required it, as cited locally.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: A confirmation or case number from the recipient.

investigation.title: Investigation
investigation.description: The review of why the event happened and what will change.

method.title: Method
method.description: root-cause-analysis, apparent-cause-analysis, failure-mode-and-effects-analysis, case-review or none.

causes.title: Causes
causes.description: The root or apparent causes identified.

strength.title: Strength
strength.description: stronger (for example forcing functions, standardized equipment), intermediate (checklists, redundancy) or weaker (training, new policy), following the action hierarchy widely used in root cause analysis.

measure.title: Measure of success
measure.description: How the organization will know the action worked.

psoSubmission.title: PSO submission
psoSubmission.description: Submission of the report to a patient safety organization, where one is used.

commonFormatsVersion.title: Common Formats version
commonFormatsVersion.description: The version of the AHRQ Common Formats used for the submission, if any.

status.description: submitted, triaged, under-investigation, action-plan, closed or not-a-safety-event.

statusHistory.title: Status history
statusHistory.description: Every status the record has had, oldest first, each one of the values of status. For an anonymous report, don't record the reporter in by.

status.description: The status the record moved to, one of this format's status values.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.description: Files that belong to the report. Keep identifiable clinical documents in the clinical record, not here.

auditTrail.title: Audit trail
auditTrail.description: Recorded actions on the report, oldest first. For an anonymous report, don't record the reporter as an actor.

extensions.description: Local fields this format doesn't define, namespaced as <namespace>:<field>.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status values of this format.
